cards.text: Saul and his son Jonathan are dead, and David has poured out his grief for them in a song (2 Samuel 1:17-27). Some time later, David doesn't just pack up and make a move. He asks the LORD first: should he go up to one of the towns of Judah?

cards.question: When David asks about going up to a town of Judah, the LORD tells him to wait.
David asks a follow-up question: where should he go? The LORD answers: go to ___.

cards.text: So David goes up to Hebron, and he doesn't go alone. Two questions, two answers, and he's on the road. Baker, I have spent LONGER than that deciding between sprinkles and chocolate chips.

cards.question: Who goes with David to Hebron?

answers.text: His two wives Ahinoam and Abigail
His father Jesse and his brothers
The prophet Samuel and the priests

cards.text: David's men come along too, every one of them with his whole household. That's not moving day, friend, that's a PARADE, and they all settle in the towns near Hebron.

cards.question: Then the men of Judah come to David in Hebron. What do they do there?

answers.text: Anoint him king over the house of Judah
Ask him to lead them against the Philistines
Hand him the crown from Saul's head

cards.question: In Hebron, the men of Judah anoint David king over every tribe of Israel.

cards.text: Then the men of Judah pass along some news. Saul fell in battle on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:1-6), and someone gave him a burial.

cards.question: The men of Judah tell David that the men of ___ buried Saul.

cards.text: So David sends messengers to Jabesh-gilead. Now remember, Saul spent day after day hunting David (1 Samuel 23:14), and me? Somebody chases me around for years, my note to his friends gets VERY lost in the mail.

cards.question: What message does David send to the men of Jabesh-gilead?

answers.text: The LORD bless you for your kindness to Saul
You should have brought Saul's body to me
Send your strongest fighters down to Hebron

cards.question: David asks the LORD to show the men of Jabesh-gilead loving devotion, and he promises to show them favor himself because of what they did.
David tells the men of Jabesh-gilead to be strong and courageous. What reason does he give them?

answers.text: Saul is dead but Judah has anointed David king
The Philistines are marching toward their town
The LORD has promised them a great victory

cards.text: Meanwhile, Saul's side is NOT just sitting around. Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, is about to make a big move.

cards.question: Abner, the commander of Saul's army, takes someone and moves him to Mahanaim. Who is it?
Abner makes Ish-bosheth king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim and Benjamin. That's king over all ___.
Ish-bosheth is forty years old when he begins to reign over Israel, and he stays king for forty years.
The house of Judah sticks with David. How long is David king in Hebron over the house of Judah?

cards.text: So now there are two kings: David in Hebron, and Ish-bosheth in Mahanaim. Hold on to your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "So David goes up to Hebron, and he doesn't go alone." / "Two questions, two answers, and he's on the road." / "Baker, I have spent LONGER than that deciding between sprinkles and chocolate chips." Only the opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke has Papa Dorin say he would hold a grudge against someone who chased him ("my note to his friends gets VERY lost in the mail"). That clashes with his character, especially in a card about David showing kindness.

rule.text: Godly character. He never holds a grudge, and his humor reflects kindness and forgiveness.

findings.problem: The joke is crammed into the same sentence as the Bible fact ("Saul spent day after day hunting David (1 Samuel 23:14), and me? Somebody chases me around for years, my note..."). It reads as a run-on, so the comparison doesn't click right away.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: Only the right answer, "The LORD bless you for your kindness to Saul," sounds like a Bible blessing. The two wrong answers are plain modern statements, so the right one stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "David asks the LORD to show the men of Jabesh-gilead loving devotion" calls David's words a request to the LORD. In the text, David's message says to the men, "Now may the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness" (2 Samuel 2:6). This is the same pattern as the Naomi example.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: Ish-bosheth's two-year reign (2 Samuel 2:10) only shows up as the hidden truth behind a False answer. No card ever tells the baker it was two years, so they leave Prep without that detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The first sentence, "So now there are two kings: David in Hebron, and Ish-bosheth in Mahanaim," only recaps cards 16 through 19 and adds nothing new. The last verse was already asked on card 19, so this card should be just the story-continues line.
